title: Ebb-and-Flow Reservoir Scheduler: elasticity-aware prefill/decode allocator
creator: Anita Patel
description: Design and implement an ebb-and-flow reservoir scheduler that dynamically apportions tokens and micro-batches between prefill and decode phases based on short-term demand signals, kernel latency probes, and attention-density heuristics. The goal is to improve tail latency and tenant fairness under mixed workloads while preserving throughput for cost-sensitive tenants. This ticket covers design, a simulator, an in-prod canary, and an initial rollout plan.
acceptance_criteria: Scheduler prototype implemented in runtime with feature flag
Simulator shows >=10% p99 latency reduction for tail-heavy mixed-tenant traces compared to baseline without throughput regression >3%
Automated smoke tests for stability under bursty traffic pass in CI
Canary rollout to 5% of Dedicated capacity with observability dashboards and rollback playbook
A short runbook describing credit exhaustion behaviors and how to adjust reservoir parameters is published
decisions: Use a token-reservoir model: each tenant has a soft reservoir (tokens/sec) and a burst reservoir (tokens) that refill on a tunable schedule
Allocate phase split points by combining: recent latency quantiles, kernel probed latency hints, and attention-density estimate from prefill metadata
Fairness: implement deficit-accounting credits (leaky-bucket style) to deprioritize noisy tenants without hard rate-limiting
Fallback policy: if kernel probe fails or KV cache hit-rate degrades, fall back to conservative phase split favoring decode to protect latency-sensitive traffic
tradeoffs: Favoring tail latency reduces aggregate throughput in some traces; we tune reservoir refill to bound throughput regression
Kernel probing adds small overhead and potential noise — we will probe adaptively and back off during instability
Per-tenant reservoirs increase scheduler state and memory; we limit to active-tenants and garbage-collect idle entries
plan_steps: 1) Design doc + parameter matrix (owners: Diego, Jonah)
2) Build discrete-event simulator to replay representative traces and sweep reservoir parameters
3) Implement runtime scheduler gate behind feature flag with a lightweight kernel-probe hook
4) Add observability: per-tenant reservoir fill-levels, phase-split ratios, kernel probe latencies
5) Run canary on dedicated pool, monitor key metrics for 48h
6) Iterate parameters and prepare gradual rollout plan

experiment_plan: Simulate three workload mixes: tail-heavy chat, bursty embeddings, and steady streaming generation
Sweep reservoir refill interval [0.1s, 0.5s, 1s], burst size [1x, 2x, 4x baseline], and attention-threshold [0.1, 0.25, 0.5]
Collect p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, kernel utilization, and tenant fairness index (Jain's index over delivered throughput)
Select conservative default minimizing p99 while keeping throughput loss <3% for best-effort tenants
metrics_targets: p99 end-to-end generation latency: reduce by >=10% on tail workloads
Tenant fairness index: increase by >=0.05 on mixed workloads
Kernel probe overhead: <0.5% added CPU or latency on average
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Reservoir starvation for small tenants under sustained bursts — Mitigation: implement minimum guaranteed credit and decay window
Risk: Probe-induced oscillation across kernel variants — Mitigation: probe damping and hysteresis before switching kernels
Risk: Increased scheduler memory pressure — Mitigation: TTL-based eviction for idle tenants and shared reservoir defaults
next_steps: Finalize conservative default parameters and add to runtime config schema
Schedule canary for 2026-03-08 on dedicated-qa pool and run 72h with alerting thresholds
PM to prepare customer communications for behavior changes affecting enterprise tenants
Design small-scale A/B against existing phased-splitter to quantify user-visible regression (if any)
